characters.name: Jesus
characters.note: Central figure; the Word made flesh who teaches, heals and is crucified and raised.

characters.name: John
characters.note: Man sent from God who baptizes and testifies to the light; distinct from John the apostle.

characters.name: Andrew
characters.note: Disciple, Simon Peter's brother, from Bethsaida.

characters.name: Simon Peter
characters.note: Disciple renamed Cephas (Peter) by Jesus.

characters.name: Philip
characters.note: Disciple from Bethsaida who brings Nathanael to Jesus.

characters.name: Nathanael
characters.note: Man from Cana who becomes a disciple.

characters.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
characters.note: Mother of Jesus at the wedding in Cana and at the cross.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
characters.note: Woman who sees the risen Jesus at the tomb.

characters.name: Mary of Bethany
characters.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus who anoints Jesus.

characters.name: Martha
characters.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.

characters.name: Lazarus
characters.note: Man from Bethany raised from the dead by Jesus.

characters.name: Nicodemus
characters.note: Pharisee and ruler who comes to Jesus by night.

characters.name: the Samaritan woman
characters.note: Woman of Sychar who talks with Jesus at Jacob's well.

characters.name: the nobleman
characters.note: Official whose son is healed at Capernaum.

characters.name: the sick man
aliases: the man who had been sick thirty-eight years
characters.note: Man healed at the pool of Bethesda.

characters.name: the man born blind
characters.note: Man born blind whom Jesus heals with mud at Siloam.

characters.name: Thomas
characters.note: Disciple who doubts the resurrection until he sees Jesus.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.note: Disciple who betrays Jesus; not to be confused with Judas, not Iscariot.

characters.name: Judas (not Iscariot)
characters.note: Disciple who asks Jesus why he will reveal himself only to his disciples.

characters.name: Pilate
characters.note: Roman governor who examines Jesus and has him crucified.

characters.name: Caiaphas
characters.note: High priest who counsels that one man should die for the people.

characters.name: Annas
characters.note: Father-in-law of Caiaphas who questions Jesus first.

characters.name: Barabbas
characters.note: Robber released instead of Jesus.

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathaea
characters.note: Disciple who asks Pilate for Jesus' body.

characters.name: Malchus
characters.note: Servant whose ear Peter cuts off.

characters.name: the maid who kept the door
characters.note: Servant woman who asks Peter if he is a disciple.

characters.name: the two angels
characters.note: Angels sitting in the tomb; shown as figures in white.

characters.name: the disciple whom Jesus loved
characters.note: Unnamed disciple at the supper, at the cross and at the empty tomb.

characters.name: the soldiers
characters.note: Roman soldiers and temple officers who arrest, mock and crucify Jesus.

characters.name: the Pharisees
characters.note: Religious leaders who oppose Jesus.

characters.name: the Jews
characters.note: Jewish leaders and crowds who debate and oppose Jesus in the Gospel's usage.

characters.name: the disciples
characters.note: Jesus' followers acting together.

characters.name: Satan
characters.note: Adversary who enters Judas; not shown as a human.

brief.era: First-century Roman Judea and Galilee, under Roman rule with a Jewish temple establishment.
brief.place: Galilee, Samaria and Jerusalem, with lakeside, village, well, pool, temple, garden and hillside settings.
brief.dress: Jewish dress of the period: tunics, outer cloaks, head coverings and sandals. Roman soldiers in military dress; Pilate in Roman governor's attire; priests in priestly robes. Jesus in plain garments, the seamless tunic at the crucifixion.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Stone water pots, nets and boats, a fire of coals, a stone-sealed rock-cut tomb with linen cloths, the temple and its porches, Jacob's well, Pharisees' phylacteries and synagogue settings, lanterns and torches at the arrest, a crown of thorns, a cross, a vine, lamps, bread and fish.
depiction_rules: Show angels in white as human-like figures seated in the tomb, not as winged beings.
Show the Holy Spirit as a dove only where the text describes it, at the baptism.
Do not depict God the Father as a human figure; show the voice from heaven by light or cloud, not a face.
Depict Satan and the devil as unseen or as a shadowy presence, not as a human figure.
Show Jesus with consistent appearance across scenes, and render the risen Jesus without special glow unless the text calls for it.
Keep the women at the tomb and the disciples as distinct individuals, not generic crowds, when named.
Portray Jewish leaders and crowds without caricature; the Gospel's conflict is with specific authorities, not a people.
